name: Trade war & tariffs
summary: Trump has threatened to double tariffs on Mexico over migration; no rate, deadline or increase in force by 19 Nov
state: President Trump threatened on 12 Nov to double tariffs on Mexico unless it stops a migrant caravan, and restated the threat on 16 Nov without a rate or deadline (KATV; Newsquawk). Mexican vehicles already face 25% duties and steel and aluminium 50%. Searches to 19 Nov found no tariff increase in force and no retaliation, so Watch holds.
for_you: Tariff threats can raise prices of imported goods and add uncertainty for businesses trading with North America.
rubric_hit: Major tariff increase threatened between large economies = Watch; none in force

sources.title: KATV — Trump threatens to double tariffs on Mexico if it fails to stop migrant caravan
Newsquawk — Trump threatens to double tariffs on Mexico

why: Tariffs raise prices, reroute supply chains and slow growth; escalation cycles hurt export-heavy economies like the UK's partners.
drivers: US tariff policy, retaliation, court rulings, trade deals, WTO disputes.

rubric.alert: Broad new tariffs in force with retaliation under way, or US average effective tariff rising sharply.
rubric.watch: New major tariffs announced or threatened between large economies.
rubric.normal: Tariff regime stable; no new major measures in the past two weeks.
